text.title: Accessibility Basics Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding the Accessibility Basics methodology. Each pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale; HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override. Background covers the POUR framework, A/AA/AAA conformance requirements, four evaluation types and their coverage, and a five-minute quick-check protocol.

section.title: Background
section.p: POUR is a teaching frame for categorizing accessibility issues, not a checklist. Treating it as a checklist produces shallow audits.

list.item: Perceivable: can users perceive all content? Examples: alt text for images, captions for video, colour contrast of 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for UI components.
Operable: can users operate all controls? Examples: full keyboard access, no keyboard traps, sufficient time limits, no seizure-inducing flashes.
Understandable: can users understand content and UI? Examples: clear language, predictable navigation, error identification and suggestion.
Robust: does it work with current and future assistive technology? Examples: valid HTML, correct ARIA usage, name-role-value on all custom components.
Level A: minimum accessibility — must have. Blocking issues for all users with disabilities.
Level AA: standard for most products — legal requirement in most jurisdictions (ADA, Section 508, AODA, EN 301 549). Target for all public-facing products.
Level AAA: enhanced accessibility — ideal but not always achievable for all content types; target where possible.

section.p: Evaluation types and what each catches:

list.item: Automated testing (axe, pa11y, Lighthouse): continuous, catches structural issues (missing alt, label, contrast, heading order, duplicate IDs).
Manual testing with keyboard-only navigation: catches focus traps, invisible focus indicators, interaction-order issues.
Assistive technology testing (NVDA, VoiceOver, TalkBack): catches ARIA misuse, dynamic content not announced, custom widget behavior.
User testing with disabled participants: catches task-completion barriers that no tool or heuristic predicts.

rule.statement: Use POUR (Perceivable / Operable / Understandable / Robust) as a categorisation frame for findings — not as a 4-item checklist. Each finding is tagged with its POUR principle.
rule.rationale: Treating POUR as a checklist produces shallow audits because the four principles are categories of failure, not discrete tests.

rule.statement: Every quick-check report pins WCAG version + level (default: 'WCAG 2.2 AA'). Agents and humans MUST cite SC numbers (e.g., 1.4.3).
rule.rationale: Agents conflate WCAG levels and produce mixed-level audits that obscure compliance status; WCAG 2.2 adds four AA criteria not in 2.1.

rule.statement: Pin "WCAG 2.2 AA" in every prompt and audit specification. Agents conflate WCAG levels and produce mixed-level audits that obscure compliance status.
rule.rationale: WCAG 2.2 adds four new success criteria not in 2.1; specifying the version prevents auditing against an outdated standard. Extends pin-wcag-version-and-level from the report to the prompt and spec that produce it.

rule.statement: When reporting scanner findings, the report MUST also state 'scanner catches ≈30% of issues; manual + AT + user testing required'. Standalone scanner reports are forbidden as the only artefact.
rule.rationale: Agents overweight scanner output; the 30% ceiling is the empirical anchor for this rule.

rule.statement: Automated scanning catches approximately 30% of accessibility issues. Manual testing catches approximately 50%. Assistive-technology testing and user testing with disabled users are required for the remaining issues.
rule.rationale: Agents overweight scanner output; the 30% ceiling is explicit and must be stated whenever scanner results are reported.

rule.statement: Pre-PR quick-check covers exactly 5 steps: tab through, 200% zoom, alt-text on one image, label on one input, axe DevTools run. Output is one report.
rule.rationale: A bounded 5-step routine is what survives team adoption; longer checklists are skipped.

rule.statement: Form inputs MUST have a visible, programmatically-associated `<label for>`. Placeholder text MUST NOT be used as the label substitute.
rule.rationale: Screen readers announce the associated label on focus; placeholder disappears on input and fails SC 1.4.3 contrast.

rule.statement: Decorative images: empty alt="" plus role="presentation". Informative images: concise description of the information conveyed. Complex images: short alt plus a long description linked via aria-describedby.
rule.rationale: Alt text must convey the same information as the image to a user who cannot see it; the correct pattern depends on the image's role in the page.

rule.statement: Wire axe-core into PR CI. A failing PR for a missing label is cheaper than a post-launch fix. Lint with eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y to catch issues at type time.
rule.rationale: Accessibility debt compounds; catching issues at PR time costs minutes, at QA costs hours, and post-launch can cost litigation.

rule.statement: If preconditions in AGENTS.md "Applies If" do not all hold, OR any "Skip If" disqualifier is true, do not run this methodology — route to the named alternative.
rule.rationale: Methodologies are pre-condition gated; running them out-of-scope produces noise and burns the agent's context budget.

rule.statement: If preconditions hold, execute the procedure in `content/04-procedure.xml` (or the rule set above when complexity is light), emit the artefact specified by `content/02-output-contract.xml`, and validate with `scripts/validate-a11y-basics.py` before returning.
rule.rationale: Tying the entry rule to the validator script closes the loop between policy and machine check.
